accessibility.text: Now that we have a grip on determinism and on one view of free will which would arguably be compatible with determinism, let’s look at the central argument against the view that free will is compatible with determinism.
pasted-image.pdf
We can lay out this puzzle in terms of the following master argument against the reality of free will.
No one has any choice about the state of the world in the distant past.
1. Free will is incompatible with determinism.
2. If Libertarianism is true, then there is no free will.
C. There is no free will.
No one has any choice about what the laws of nature are.
If determinism is true, then the state of the world in the distant past + the laws of nature necessitate every future action.
The master argument against the reality of free will
pasted-image.pdf
A compatibility believer in free will rejects premise (1). An incompatibilist believer in free will rejects premise (2).
pasted-image.pdf
This is the consequence argument.
No one has any choice about the combination of the state of the world in the distant past + the laws of nature.
